Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
452 PM PST Tue Nov 24 2026

.SYNOPSIS...24/115 PM.

Warming temperatures and dry weather is expected most of the week
due to a predominant offshore flow pattern. Temperatures will 
peak on Thanksgiving and Friday with some gusty northeast winds at
times, then cooling will begin over the weekend. There is a 
possibility of a large storm system around the middle of next 
week.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-FRI)...24/141 PM.

The next Pacific storm is moving into northern California this
afternoon. This system may just barely clip the northern portion
of SLO County this evening but any rain amounts would likely be
under a tenth of an inch. Otherwise, the predominant weather
feature for southern California will be the increasing offshore
pressure gradients, particularly across the usual Santa Ana
favored areas across LA/Ventura Counties. Gradients already
reached close to -4mb from the east today and models indicate 
they will peak around -6mb by Thursday morning. At the same time
gradients from the north will be increasing as well, possibly to
around -6.5mb, so there will be a significant north wind component
as well. In these circumstances the north component tends to
create stronger northerly winds into the LA Valleys and less wind
across the western parts of Ventura County. So this Santa Ana may
have a slightly different look to it compared to typical Santa
Anas.

In any case, the Santa Ana winds along with the building ridge 
over the state will push temperatures into the 80s on Thursday and
Friday in many coast/valley areas of LA/Ventura Counties and well
into the 70s along the Central Coast. At least low end wind 
advisories are a good bet both days across parts of LA/Ventura
Counties.

.LONG TERM (SAT-TUE)...24/206 PM.

Dry but cooler weather is expected Sunday as the ridge shifts east
in response to the next storm system moving into the Pac NW. The
system will mainly impact northern California but the tail end of
the storm will likely drop some light rain through southern 
California Sunday night into Monday. Rain amounts are projected to
be mostly under a half inch.

A second and much stronger storm is likely right on the heels of
the previous one late Tuesday into Wednesday. Models have been
consistent the last few cycles indicating at least a moderate
storm and potentially strong with widespread rain amounts of at
least 1-2 inches and upslope areas as much as 2-5 inches over a
6-8 hour period. Neither of these storms are particularly cold so
any snow would likely be above 8000 feet.

&&

.AVIATION...25/0052Z.

At 0002Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer or marine inversion.

At KSMX, KSBP, and KPRB, there is a 30-50% chance of showers and
MVFR cigs from 10Z-15Z Wed. High confidence in VFR conditions for
all other sites through the period,

KLAX...High confidence in VFR conditions through the period. There
is a 30% chance that the east wind component reaches 6 kt between
06Z Wed and 21Z Thu. 

KBUR...High confidence in VFR conditions through the period.

&&

.MARINE...24/121 PM.

For the Outer Waters, moderate to high confidence in current
forecast. Tonight through Friday, high confidence in combination
of Small Craft Advisory (SCA) level winds and seas. During this
time period, seas will peak between 14 and 18 feet on Wednesday.
For Friday night through Sunday, high confidence in winds
remaining below SCA levels, but there is a 50-70% chance of SCA
level seas continuing. 

For the Inner Waters north of Point Sal, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Tonight through Friday, high 
confidence in combination of SCA level winds and seas. During this
time period, seas will peak between 13 and 16 feet on Wednesday. 
For Friday night through Sunday, high confidence in winds 
remaining below SCA levels, but a 40-60% chance of SCA level seas 
continuing. 

For the Inner Waters south of Point Conception, moderate to high
confidence in current forecast. Through tonight, high confidence
in winds and seas remaining below SCA levels. For Wednesday
through Thursday, high confidence in SCA level winds, specifically
across the western half of the Santa Barbara Channel on Wednesday
and from Point Mugu to Santa Monica on Thursday. Additionally,
there is a 40-60% chance of widespread SCA level seas Wednesday
through Thursday. For Friday through Sunday, winds and seas are
expected to remain below SCA for most areas. The only exception
will be the western half of the Santa Barbara Channel with a 50%
chance of SCA level winds Sunday afternoon and evening.

&&

.BEACHES...24/120 PM.

A large, long period, west swell will move into the coastal
waters today and peak on Wednesday and Thursday. This large swell
will combine with very high tides to bring significant surf to 
the area as well as significant coastal flooding.

The highest surf and most significant coastal flooding issues are
expected across the Central Coast as well as the beaches of
Ventura county. Elsewhere, the surf and coastal flooding issues
are a bit less, but still concerning. There will be many, strong
rip currently nearly everywhere, strong long shore currents, a
risk of sneaker waves, large shore pound, coastal erosion and
potential for breaking waves in the harbor entrances. 

Please check out LAXCFWLOX for the latest details about all of the
current advisories and warnings in effect.
